tagline: Two Versailles Road connections lead toward the limestone fences of Old Frankfort Pike
intro: Van Meter, Rice and Elkchester roads form a branched scenic route in Fayette County, connecting Versailles Road with Old Frankfort Pike. The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet records 6.295 miles in the designation. At the Versailles Road end is Keeneland; Manchester Farm, on its northern boundary, has rolling hills and a barn topped by blue-and-white cupolas.
The state designated these roads on November 20, 1996. The land beside Keeneland had already changed from family acreage to a racing landmark: in 1935, Jack Keene sold 147.6 acres for a new track.

From Versailles Road, Van Meter Road joins Rice Road. Rice also has its own Versailles Road connection; KY 1969 continues along Rice and Elkchester roads to Old Frankfort Pike. There, the adjoining National Scenic Byway offers hardwood tree cover and dry-laid limestone fences, features identified in its designation report.

moments.title: Keeneland
moments.text: Keeneland began with land held by the Keen/Keene family for five generations. In 1935, Jack Keene sold 147.6 acres to the Keeneland Association for a model racetrack. The racecourse began its April and October meets in 1936. In 1986, it became a National Historic Landmark for its part in the growth of horse racing and the sport’s revival in Lexington. The business also includes a horse auction complex and a reference library. The track changed its racing surface to Polytrack in 2006, then returned to dirt in summer 2014. A turf course had been installed in 1985.

moments.title: Manchester Farm
moments.text: The barn’s blue-and-white cupolas identify Manchester Farm on Keeneland’s northern boundary. Its earlier name, Manchester Springs Plantation, came from a creek crossing the property. In 1804, Francis Keen passed 200 acres to his son. The family retained the land for five generations before Jack Keene’s 1935 sale supplied acreage for the racetrack. In November 2022, Keeneland announced its purchase of the historic farm from Calumet Farm. At the time of the purchase, Keeneland president Shannon Arvin said the association had acquired neighboring properties to preserve the track’s setting and support racing and sales.

moments.title: Old Frankfort Pike
moments.text: Old Frankfort Pike’s dry-laid limestone fences continue for miles beneath a canopy of hardwood trees. Its National Scenic Byway designation arrived in 2021, following a nomination sponsored by the Lexington-Frankfort Scenic Corridor, Inc. The nonprofit had formed in 1988 to advance preservation and conservation in the corridor. The designated 15.5-mile section passes through six National Register rural historic districts. Its designation report describes diversified agriculture alongside the international equine industry. That protected road section stretches from Duckers Station Road in Woodford County to Wolf Run Creek in Fayette County, just outside Lexington.
